dct_description_sm:
A screenline (e.g. LN02, LN10) is made up of several stations placed to count east-west or north-south travel, which in total, capture all major travel routes across the imaginary screenline. The screenlines are located along geographical barriers, i.e. rivers, greenbelt – generally where several major transportation facilities are the main flow. To be truly representative of the flow, there is a station at each intersecting road, transit, and bike/walkway path on the screenline.
 

Date created:  June 29, 2026    
Update frequency: As required
Accuracy: Not intended to represent exact location on the ground


Attributes:

  • SL_NUM (Screenline Number)
  • SL_TEXT (Screenline Text ID)
  • CORDON_EN (Cordon - screenlines or groups of screenlines that describe an area of interest (English text))
  • CORDON_FR (Cordon - screenlines or groups of screenlines that describe an area of interest (French text))
  • NAME_EN (Screenline name (English text))
  • NAME_FR (Screenline name (French text))
  • SEASON_EN (Season that the traffic count was captured (English text))
  • SEASON_FR (Season that the traffic count was captured (French text))
  • COUNTYEAR_EN ((Both = Count Collection during All Years / Even = Count Collection during Even Years / Odd = Count Collection during
  • Odd Years) - describes when the count takes place (English text))
  • COUNTYEAR_FR (Les deux = Comptage à chaque année / Paires = Comptage pendant les années paires / Impaires = Comptage pendant les années impaires) - describes when the count takes place (French text))
  • CHANGE_EN (English text describing a change to a screenline)
  • CHANGE_FR (French text describing a change to a screenline)
  • YEAR (Year representing the version of the screenline feature)
  • STATUS_EN (Latest – English text describing the data as the most recent captured) 
  • STATUS_FR (Dernier en date – French text describing the data as the most recent captured)
